subject.title: feat(workspace): lint and auto-fix code fences in markdown at write time

question: Should OpenClaw add Markdown code-fence hygiene to workspace file writes, and should that behavior be default auto-fix, warn/doctor-only, opt-in, or outside the core write path?
rationale: The request changes write semantics for user-authored Markdown and adds config/API surface; prior implementation attempts exposed parser correctness risk, so automation should not choose the permanent policy.

options.title: Require Warn Or Opt-In Design First
options.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer-approved design avoids silent default rewrites and proves parser safety against nested fence examples.

options.title: Approve Default Auto-Fix
options.body: Allow a future PR to mutate workspace Markdown by default with explicit config docs, skip API, parser-backed tests, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Reject Core Write-Time Mutation
options.body: Close or redirect the idea toward docs linting, doctor lint, Skill Workshop guidance, or a plugin/workflow outside core writes.

recommendation.title: Require Warn Or Opt-In Design First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a maintainer-approved design avoids silent default rewrites and proves parser safety against nested fence examples.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent overlap across the gateway protocol/workspace surface and shared Markdown helper consolidation.
